title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Play music through your speakers while games and calls use your headset. From the Windows system tray, SonicRoute lets you choose a playback device and microphone for each app and adjust its volume.

downloadIntro: Choose **Lite** for Windows audio, **Full** to add Android and AirPlay, or **Legacy** for PC audio on an x64 system with .NET Framework 4.8. The table lists downloads for {release} and links to the Microsoft Store editions.

steps: **Open SonicRoute.** Run the EXE (extract the ZIP first for Legacy). Double-click the SonicRoute icon in the system tray to open the main window.

**Route an app.** In Settings, choose which devices to show. Play audio in an app, then single-click the tray icon. Expand the app’s row in the quick panel to choose an output. Drag its slider to adjust its volume.

**Try the mouse wheel.** Scroll over the tray icon to adjust the current app’s volume. By default, SonicRoute looks for an audio session in the foreground app first, then in the last foreground app that had one. Hold Alt and scroll to switch the app’s output, or hold Shift and scroll to adjust the volume of the system’s default playback device.
commandNote: The `sr` command sends a rule name or ID to a running copy of SonicRoute over a named pipe. Start SonicRoute once to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. You can now call `sr` from a script, AutoHotkey or Stream Deck. If SonicRoute is closed, `sr` returns an error. See {faq}.

releaseSummary:
Full can now receive AirPlay audio (PCM, ALAC, AAC-LC and AAC-ELD) and mirror a screen at its original aspect ratio using a receiver written in C#. Set an optional pairing code, keep the mirror on top or press F11 for full screen. Drag audio to a PC output, an Android phone’s speaker or a Bluetooth device connected to the phone. Android and AirPlay support H.265 (HEVC). Android falls back to H.264 if the encoder cannot start. You can choose Android audio and video decoders. SonicRoute checks the available encoders when you open the device settings and sends gamepad input only to the focused video window.

Android pairing now puts the QR code (refreshed every two minutes) beside the manual pairing code. Reconnecting or refreshing a device checks its identity and looks for its current address and port on the local network. SonicRoute preserves a manually entered address if the search fails and can restore settings for a previously paired device.

All editions now have separate options to keep the mic indicator on screen when all microphones are muted or when the default recording device is muted. Configuration tools share one row. Long app lists render only the visible rows once the list exceeds 20 entries. SonicRoute combines on-screen updates and frees decoded PNG source data, backs up settings to `config.json.bak` and records diagnostics when errors occur. Full also releases unused video textures and leaves garbage collection to the runtime when a window closes. Lite is available separately in the Microsoft Store, and all editions include an offline copy of the GPL-3.0-only license. See {history} for details.

features: **Choose where each app plays and records.** In the quick panel, Ctrl-click a playback device to add or remove it. Shift-click to select a range. All editions can play through several PC outputs at once. Full can also include outputs on a connected Android phone.

**See what’s playing and adjust its volume.** Live level meters show which apps are playing, each with its own volume slider. Scroll over the tray icon to adjust the current app’s volume, or use a hotkey to mute and unmute your microphones.

**Automate routine changes.** Choose one of {triggerCount} triggers and build a sequence from {actionCount} available actions. When a game starts, a rule can switch to your headset and open voice chat. You can also run a saved rule from a terminal or script with `sr`.

**Use Android and AirPlay on your PC (Full).** Play an Android app’s audio on your PC, send PC audio to your phone, or use an Android app in its own virtual display. SonicRoute also receives AirPlay audio and screen mirroring from Apple devices. Browse an Android phone’s shared storage and transfer multiple files in either direction.
developmentNotes: For audio from Android to your PC, choose Opus (default) or uncompressed PCM. Each phone has three latency modes: Ultra-low latency, Balanced (default), and Stable. Changes take effect the next time you start an audio stream from that phone.
If the Android encoder supports it, the virtual display adjusts its video bitrate as connection conditions change.
useCaseNames: **Listen to music or watch a video while gaming**
**Switch to a headset when a game starts**
**Step away from a call or speak privately**
**Stream with OBS or record a tutorial**
**Listen to a phone or use its apps on your PC**
useCaseActions: Adjust voice chat (such as Discord) without changing the game’s volume. You can also send the game and the chat to different outputs.
Send music to your speakers and keep the game in your headset. Scroll over the SonicRoute icon to adjust the target app’s volume, or hold Alt and scroll to switch its output.
Create a rule that switches to the headset, sets the volume to 40% and opens voice chat when the game starts. Use an exit rule to switch back to the speakers.
The default shortcut, Ctrl+Shift+N, toggles mute for all microphones. Enable the persistent on-screen indicator to see when they’re muted.
Send the apps you want to record to a separate physical or virtual output, then select that output in your recording software. Leave chats and notifications on another output.

Play an Android game in a virtual display on your PC, with H.265 video on supported devices. Gamepad input goes to the game only while its virtual display window has focus. Choose your PC speakers in the quick panel. Smart Volume helps even out sudden changes in loudness.

faqQuestions: What happens to app routing and volume when I exit SonicRoute?
How much CPU or battery does SonicRoute use in the background?
faqAnswers: Windows keeps each app’s primary PC playback device, recording device and the volume of existing audio sessions. Playback on additional outputs stops when you exit SonicRoute. Keep SonicRoute running to use hotkeys, tray controls, automation, phone audio, screen mirroring or clipboard sync.

Full and Lite require the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime for the build’s architecture. The Store editions require the x64 runtime. Legacy uses .NET Framework 4.8. Archived .NET 8 builds are still available but no longer receive updates.

SonicRoute relies on Windows notifications and checks process state once a second when needed. It releases data it no longer uses. CPU use and battery impact depend on your system and what you’re doing.
